content.title: Michael B. Jordan's Oscars Best Actor Speech Is Absolutely Perfect
content.text: Michael B. Jordan is going from sinner to Oscar winner. The actor takes homeMichael B. Jordan's Oscars Best Actor Speech Is Absolutely Perfect0 seconds of 1 minute, 14 secondsVolume 0%Michael B. Jordan's Oscars Best Actor Speech Is Absolutely PerfectMichael B. Jordan is going from sinner to winner at the 2026 Oscars. The Sinners star earned his first-ever Academy Award for his dual portrayals of twin brothers Smoke and Stack in the horror blockbuster, earning a thunderous response as he accepted his Best Actor statuette at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles March 15. “Thank you, everybody in this room and everybody at home, for supporting me over my career. I feel it,” he said during the ceremony hosted by Conan O’Brien. “I know you guys want me to do well, and I want to do that because you guys bet on me, so thank you for keep betting on me. I'm gonna keep stepping up, and I'm gonna keep being the best version of myself I can be." And Michael—who was also nominated alongside Marty Supreme’s Timothée Chalamet, One Battle After Another’s Leonardo DiCaprio, Blue Moon’s Ethan Hawke and The Secret Agent’s Wagner Moura—offered a special shoutout to his parents, including his father, who traveled overseas to witness his son's career achievement. "Y'all know how I feel about my mother, and my father's here," he continued. "My dad came in from Ghana to be here." The 39-year-old’s triumph also makes him the sixth Black performer to win Best Actor, joining the ranks of Sidney Poitier, Denzel Washington, Jamie Foxx, Forest Whitaker and Will Smith before him. He recognized his predecessors as well as Halle Berry—the first Black woman to win Best Actress—describing the trailblazing group as "giants."Heading into Oscars night, Michael, 39, had strong momentum in the Best Actor race. After all, the All My Children alum was honored at the 2026 Actor Awards just two weeks earlier, shouting out his fellow nominees after ascending to the stage. “I'm so honored and privileged to be nominated in categories with people and actors and humans that I love,” he said at the time. “I love their work and what you contribute to our craft. This ride has been unbelievable.”Kevin Winter/Getty ImagesDuring award season, Michael also praised the cast and crew he worked with on the Ryan Coogler film, highlighting the collaborative energy on set. “I think it’s one of those things where you all get on set and everybody is collectively doing the work together and everybody’s vibing off one another,” he told E! News in January. “It’s a family environment.” And the movie’s success has only enriched his fondness for the project, as Michael noted, “We’re really grateful and happy that everybody still loves the work that we’ve done.”To see all the winners at the 2026 Academy Awards, read on…Best PictureBugonia F1 Frankenstein Hamnet Marty Supreme WINNER: One Battle After Another The Secret Agent Sentimental Value Sinners Train DreamsActress in a Leading RoleWINNER: Jessie Buckley - Hamnet Rose Byrne - If I Had Legs I'd Kick You Kate Hudson - Song Sung Blue Renate Reinsve - Sentimental Value Emma Stone - BugoniaActor in a Leading RoleTimothée Chalamet - Marty Supreme Leonardo DiCaprio - One Battle After Another Ethan Hawke - Blue Moon WINNER: Michael B.
